key_sections: s.47 (endangered/threatened species listing); s.48 (restricted activities requiring permits); s.49 (recovery plans); s.50 (bioprospecting); s.77–86 (licensing); s.92 (offences involving endangered species); s.95A (poisoning); Part XII ss.97–103 (international treaties/CITES)
species_categories: Mammals; birds; reptiles; amphibians; fish; invertebrates; all wildlife species listed in Sixth Schedule and CITES Appendices
restriction_type: Fully protected (no take without permit); prohibited commercial trade; restricted activities require KWS permit; bioprospecting permit required
notes: Primary legislation. Sixth Schedule lists 245 nationally threatened species. Highest penalties in Africa: up to life imprisonment for most serious offences. 2025 Amendment Act (No.24 of 2025) expanded marine wildlife claims committee. New Bill to repeal and replace under development as of 2025.

key_sections: Part V (biodiversity conservation); s.42 (biological diversity); s.43 (in-situ conservation); s.44 (ex-situ conservation); s.45 (genetic resources access); s.49 (forests); s.55 (wetlands — prohibits alien/indigenous species introduction without authorisation)
species_categories: All biological/genetic resources; invasive alien species; threatened/endangered species
restriction_type: Access permit required for genetic resource collection/export; prohibition on introducing species into water bodies without authorisation; NEMA may ban access to threatened species
notes: Subsidiary: Access & Benefit Sharing Regulations 2006 (L.N.160/2006); ABS Regulations 2025 (L.N.19/2025); Biodiversity Regulations 2023. Aligns with Convention on Biological Diversity and Nagoya Protocol.

key_sections: s.42 (prohibited gear/methods); s.45 (declaration of endangered fish species); s.46 (marine mammals — directed fishing prohibited; incidental catch must be immediately released); s.47 (Marine Protected Areas); s.48 (Fisheries Impact Assessments); s.63 (import live fish — permit required); s.64 (export live fish — permit required)
species_categories: Marine mammals; sea turtles; fish species declared endangered by Director-General; marine protected area species
restriction_type: Prohibition on directed fishing for marine mammals; mandatory release of incidentally caught marine mammals; Director-General may declare fish species endangered; import/export live fish requires permit
enforcement_institution: Kenya Fisheries Service (KeFS); Kenya Maritime Authority (KMA)
notes: All Kenyan maritime zones declared a marine mammal and turtle sanctuary (carried forward from predecessor Fisheries Act Cap.378). 'Fish' defined broadly to include any marine/aquatic animal or plant, shells, corals, reptiles, marine mammals.

key_sections: s.40 (protected tree species — Cabinet Secretary may gazette any tree species as protected on KEFRI advice); s.46 (quarrying prohibited in areas with rare/endangered species or sacred trees); s.60 (import/export forest products — permit required); s.64 (prohibited activities in public forests without licence)
species_categories: Tree species gazetted as protected; forest-dependent flora and fauna
restriction_type: Gazette-listed trees cannot be felled, cut, damaged, removed, traded or exported; all forest produce activities require licence; import/export permits required
notes: No fixed schedule of protected trees — protection through Cabinet Secretary Gazette orders on KEFRI advice. Repealed Forests Act No.3 of 2005 and Timber Act Cap.386.

key_sections: s.3 (seed imports — licence required); s.8 (protected crop zones against injurious cross-pollination); s.14 (Cabinet Secretary may prohibit/regulate seed exports); s.19–26 (Plant Breeders Rights); s.28 (Plant Genetic Resources Centre)
species_categories: All seed species; plant varieties including indigenous plant genetic resources
restriction_type: All seed imports require KEPHIS licence; Cabinet Secretary may prohibit seed exports; exotic varieties require risk assessment before introduction
enforcement_institution: Kenya Plant Health Inspectorate Service (KEPHIS); Kenya Standing Technical Committee on Imports and Exports
notes: Companion legislation: Plant Protection Act Cap.324 — empowers Cabinet Secretary to prohibit/restrict import of any plants; intentional introduction of alien plant species requires Standing Technical Committee approval.

key_sections: s.4 (NBA establishment); s.5 (NBA mandate over GMO transfer/handling/use); s.18–25 (contained use permits); s.26–32 (environmental release permits); s.33–40 (import/export/transit of GMOs — NBA prior approval); s.52 (offences: up to KES 20M fine or 10 years imprisonment)
species_categories: Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) of all types
restriction_type: All GMO activities (import/export/transit/contained use/environmental release/commercialisation) require prior NBA approval; Government cabinet ban on GM food imports (November 2012) still in force subject to NBA processes
enforcement_institution: National Biosafety Authority (NBA); KEPHIS; NEMA; KEBS; Directorate of Veterinary Services
notes: No fixed prohibited species list — permit-based system. Unauthorised GMO handling is criminal offence.

key_sections: WCMA Part XII ss.97–103 (treaties implementation); L.N.241/2017 (Implementation of Treaties Regulations); L.N.242/2017 (Protection of Endangered/Threatened Ecosystems, Habitats and Species Regulations)
species_categories: All species listed in CITES Appendix I (trade prohibited/heavily restricted); Appendix II (trade regulated with permits); Appendix III (national protection)
restriction_type: Appendix I: commercial international trade prohibited; Appendix II: trade permitted only with CITES permit from KWS; Appendix III: import requires CITES certificate of origin
enforcement_institution: Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) as CITES Management Authority; Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) at borders/ports
notes: Kenya ratified CITES 1978. Kenya hosts CITES Secretariat in Nairobi. CITES Appendix I species are de facto incorporated into WCMA Sixth Schedule protections.

key_sections: Powers to prohibit/restrict importation of any plants, plant pests, and associated material; prevention of introduction and spread of plant pests and diseases
species_categories: All plant species (especially exotic/alien plants); plant pests; invasive plants
restriction_type: Import prohibition or restriction of specified plants/materials; intentional introduction of alien plant species requires Standing Technical Committee approval
notes: Under review 2022–2023 to strengthen regulatory framework.

key_sections: Maritime safety; prevention of marine pollution; preservation of marine environment
species_categories: Marine species and ecosystems (indirectly through pollution prevention)
restriction_type: Prevention of marine pollution; enforcement of shipping safety and environmental standards in Kenyan waters
notes: Relevant to illegal wildlife trade through seaports; coordinates with KeFS and KWS on marine enforcement.

key_sections: Protection of natural heritage including paleontological specimens and endemic species of scientific value
restriction_type: No removal/export of listed natural heritage items without National Museums of Kenya authorisation
notes: Administers natural heritage including Type specimens of Kenya endemic species.

species_categories: Wildlife trafficking networks (applied to illegal wildlife trade)
restriction_type: Criminal enterprise prosecution for organised wildlife trafficking
enforcement_institution: Director of Public Prosecutions; Kenya Police Service; KWS
notes: Used in prosecution of high-level wildlife trafficking syndicates alongside WCMA.

law_name: Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Act
key_sections: Asset recovery and anti-money laundering provisions
restriction_type: Seizure and forfeiture of assets derived from illegal wildlife trade
enforcement_institution: Asset Recovery Agency; Kenya Revenue Authority; Kenya Financial Intelligence Centre
notes: Applied when illegal wildlife trade generates criminal proceeds.
